scenario_detail: Not a real historical incident. Drift physics, spill mask, vessel identities and AIS gaps are real; the scene is relocated to a location with confirmed 2024 vessel traffic because CMEMS forcing for Indian waters is not yet available.

factors.label: Proximity to origin
factors.explanation: Closest approach to the reconstructed origin was 2.6 km.

factors.label: Timing overlap
factors.explanation: No overlap: observed 2024-01-06 23:48Z, outside the 2024-01-02 12:00Z to 2024-01-03 00:00Z window.

factors.label: Trajectory consistency
factors.explanation: Not computable: only one observed position is available (GFW tracks dataset returns 403 for this token).

factors.label: Drift agreement
factors.explanation: Not computable: only one observed position is available (GFW tracks dataset returns 403 for this token).

factors.label: AIS discrepancy
factors.explanation: No AIS gap detected inside the window.

provenance.drift_forcing: OpenDrift bundled NorKyst sample (western Norway, Nov 2015)
provenance.georeferencing: Path B - assumed anchor and pixel size, no geotransform
provenance.vessel_tracks: REAL single observation per vessel (gap-event position). Full tracks unavailable: GET /v3/vessels/{id}/tracks returns HTTP 403 for dataset public-global-all-tracks:latest with this token.
provenance.track_quality: single_observation - heading and drift agreement not computable

transposition.reason: GFW holds no vessel data for the NorKyst sample domain in 2015; drift shape and scale are real, map position and epoch are moved.

provenance.candidate_source: loitering events (date range widened to 2024, box unchanged)
provenance.candidate_caveat: Gap events in the 12h window: 0. The one gap-event object was type=gear (a buoy), not a vessel. The listed vessel comes from a loitering event at the SAME origin box with the date range widened to 2024; it therefore scores 0 on timing overlap, which is why its total is low. The origin box was never widened.
